actor: Agent-framework and hyperscaler agent-runtime maintainer and runtime-security lead (a top-tier platform team such as LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, or Bedrock AgentCore)
job: Wiring an inline action-level risk classifier into the framework's tool-execution path so every tool call is scored or blocked at runtime.
outcome: A released, not demo-only, first-class runtime guardrail that classifies agent actions per tool call, ideally shipped default-on.
motivation: Frameworks trust tool calls today; the week's memory-poisoning and unpatched-vuln disclosures make closing the action-authorization gap a competitive necessity.

task.who: the framework's agent-runtime and security-tooling maintainers
task.what: wire an action-scoring interceptor into the tool-call path
task.where: the runtime tool-execution and interceptor layer
task.why: tool calls are trusted, leaving actions unauthorized and exposed
task.how: adopt SingGuard-class open weights or an equivalent inline classifier

actor: Open-weight AI-safety guardrail-model research and release team (the SingGuard-NSFA-class safety lab and its open-weight peers)
job: Releasing and hardening small, fast open-weight guardrail models that score agent actions against a prompt-injection-to-permission-misuse risk taxonomy.
outcome: A widely inspectable, drop-in action-classifier reference implementation frameworks can adopt, removing the build-it-yourself barrier to first-class action guarding.
motivation: Establishing their weights and risk taxonomy as the reference control makes inline action-level guarding the industry norm.

task.who: the safety lab's guardrail-model research and release engineering
task.what: open-source and harden action-scoring guardrail weights
task.why: to remove the build-it-yourself barrier and set the reference
task.how: open weights at 0.8B-9B, ~50ms inference, seven-category taxonomy

actor: Enterprise agent-platform security and governance lead deploying agents at scale
job: Mandating inline action-level tool-call gating as a required control and piloting SingGuard-class interceptors on production agent tool calls.
outcome: Deployment requirements and reference integrations that make runtime action-gating table-stakes, pressuring frameworks to ship it first-class and default-on.
motivation: Memory-poisoning and unpatched-AI-vuln disclosures make trusting agent tool calls an unacceptable security and compliance risk.

task.what: mandate inline action-level tool-call gating in deployments
task.where: internal agent platforms and production tool-call pipelines
task.why: trusting agent tool calls is now an unacceptable risk
task.how: SingGuard-class interceptors, security-review gates, and procurement requirements
